question.:question/problem: Calculate $\int (\frac{1}{5+x}+\frac{1}{-8-x})\,\text{d}x.$ Assume that $K$ is an arbitrary positive constant.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{5+x}+\frac{1}{-8-x})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{5+x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{-8-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|5+x|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|-8-x|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{5+x}{-8-x}|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{5+x}{-8-x}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.

domain.K: positive arbitrary separately on each real connected component

\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{4x+3}+\frac{1}{4x-3})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{4x+3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{4x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x+3|+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4x-3|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|(4x+3)(4x-3)|+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|(4x+3)(4x-3)|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.
